docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against a model of the chip, a fuzzer that corrupts what the chip sends back, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a protocol model of the chip ( tests/mock_at25040b.hpp ). The model is written from the datasheet on its own: it includes none of the driver's headers and carries its own opcodes, status bits, array sizes and Table 6-4, each with its datasheet page, and tests/test_model.cpp cross-checks the two maps with static_assert (handbook KB-TST-030). It models the opcodes with A8 on the AT25040B, invalid opcodes that leave SO in high impedance, the write enable latch (set by WREN only with WP high, cleared by WRDI whatever WP does and at the end of every write cycle), sequential READ with roll-over, WRITE that wraps inside its page, a self-timed write cycle in simulated time during which only RDSR works and reads 0xFF, block protection that refuses writes into the protected top and survives a power cycle. The faults are the ones a board can produce or the datasheet names: MISO floating high, stuck low, echoing MOSI or random; HOLD strapped to CS; WP tied low; a WRITE the chip silently ignores; a cell that does not take its value; a write cycle that never ends; failed, lost and replaced transfers; a failing WP pin. They build with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , -pedantic-errors and warnings as errors, as ISO C++20 ( CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF ), on GCC and Clang, with the standard library's own bounds checks on ( _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS , libc++ hardening). at25040b_host_tests runs 74 test cases; with the Kconfig, version, install, Doxygen, host-example, compile-fail and fuzz-corpus tests CTest runs 16 tests. The target at25040b_header_checks compiles each public header alone as -std=c++20 -pedantic-errors and asserts the dialect; the Cortex-M cross-build compiles the same units, and the ESP32 example compiles at25040b_cxx20_check.cpp the same way inside ESP-IDF, which otherwise builds in a newer GNU dialect. cmake -S . -B build -DAT25040B_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_at25040b.cpp The lifecycle (no I/O before the start, a retried start, re-probe), Validate() , the identity check against every bus fault, reads (chunks, A8, verification, waiting out a write cycle, a glitched status), writes (page split, a 512-byte whole-array write, WP, block protection, an ignored WRITE, a stuck cell, a cycle that never ends, a failing WP pin, the smaller parts), the status and block protection, logging tests/test_bus_faults.cpp Every transfer and every WP pin write of every operation, EnsureInitialized() included, fails in turn and each returns Bus (a transfer) or Pin (a pin write) with WP parked; every transfer of a write is lost in turn and none yields Ok without the data tests/test_model.cpp The model's map against the driver's, at compile time: opcodes, status bits, sizes, Table 6-4 for every part and level tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( at25040b_fuzz_at25040b_corpus ), see below tests/test_errors.cpp Every chip-specific value (16 to 21) is returned by a real call tests/test_version.cpp The version getters follow the generated header (also against a 9.8.7 probe) tests/test_kconfig.cpp KconfigDefaults() with and without CONFIG_ values tests/compile_fail/ Code that must not compile, each for its EXPECT: diagnostic: a port without DelayUs() , a void GpioSet() , a class that is not a port, a Transfer() with a narrower length or without noexcept , a DelayUs(uint16_t) tests/mock_at25040b.hpp The chip model; the mock ports over it are in mock_at25040b_bus.hpp tests/check_version_copy.cmake _config/Doxyfile carries the CMake version examples/host/ The host example, built with the test flags and run ( at25040b_host_example ) tests/check_install.cmake Installs into a scratch prefix and builds tests/install_consumer/ with find_package(at25040b) tests/check_doxygen.cmake Doxygen with _config/Doxyfile and warnings as errors, when doxygen is installed The model does not reproduce the chip's electrical behaviour, its real write cycle time (it uses 3 ms) or what a partly clocked WRITE does: see Status and limitations . Fuzz tests ¶ Everything the driver receives comes from MISO, so MISO is what a noisy cable, an unplugged module or a broken chip controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_at25040b.cpp lets libFuzzer choose a configuration, then up to 64 driver calls, and on every transfer what the bus does: pass the model's reply, fail the transfer, lose it (the chip never sees it, MISO floats), flip bits of the reply or replace it; on every WP pin write, pass or fail it. Between calls it changes the board: MISO floating, stuck low, echoing or noisy, HOLD strapped to CS, WP tied low, an ignored WRITE, a stuck cell, a slow or running write cycle, the block protection, a power cycle. A transfer the bus rather than the chip answered counts as tampered. After every call the target checks the driver's promises and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a failed call returns an Error the enum defines (never one documented as not returned) and T{} ; before EnsureInitialized() no call makes a transfer or a pin write, and InvalidArgument means nothing was sent; nothing is ever written outside the requested range; only Write() changes the array and only SetBlockProtection() changes BP1:BP0; a call never returns Ok for bytes the chip does not hold : an Ok from Read() or Write() matches the chip unless two transfers of the call were tampered (one, with Verify::None ); the input chooses Verify::None or Verify::ReadBack for the reads and writes; with check_write_enable , EnsureInitialized() never returns Ok on a dead bus or with WP tied low unless a transfer was tampered; WP is always parked after a call , unless the last pin write failed; an Ok call leaves the write enable latch clear if it found it clear, unless a transfer was tampered. The fuzzer found two bugs before the first commit, both fixed with a unit test and a regress-* input each: With the write enable latch already set (a WREN before an MCU reset) and WP held low, the identity check's "WREN, then WEN = 1" passed although WP had blocked the WREN. The driver now clears the latch first ( regress-wen-preset-wp-low ). One status read that looked idle (a lost transfer reading 0x00) while a write cycle ran let Read() go ahead; the busy chip ignored both READs, both copies read 0xFF, and Read() returned Ok with wrong bytes. An idle status now counts only when a second read confirms it ( regress-idle-glitch-during-cycle ). # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DAT25040B_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DAT25040B_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_at25040b ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_at25040b -max_total_time = 300 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_at25040b The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_at25040b , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_at25040b/ on GCC and Clang: the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise ( regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request (job Host quality / fuzz ). After the fixes, ten minutes of local fuzzing (9.6 million runs, 451 coverage edges) broke no promise; after the move to spans, the Pin error and ReadRawStatus() , 200 s more (2.28 million runs, 478 edges) broke none. Quality gates ¶ The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high This driver (local) Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 highest 11 ( waitIdle() ) Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 within the limit Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 within the limit Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % 99.5 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % 98.4 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) 99.2 % Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report clean in CI Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise 2.28 million runs in 200 s locally, clean The local figures are GCC 15 and gcovr 8.7 with the CI's options; CI uses GCC 14. The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DAT25040B_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc/*.hpp src/*.ipp # list the files: lizard skips .ipp in a directory # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DAT25040B_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target at25040b_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. The README's example is a generated copy of the same file; kokeb-docs check fails when it drifts. CI workflows ¶ Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), figure and generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check, Lighthouse Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type, with the repository root as the driver's component, and lints the example sources. The gate needs it too. The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of kokeb-labs/ci-tools at @v1 . On hardware ¶ The driver is not verified on hardware yet. The ESP32 example ( Examples ) is a first bench test: it checks the chip, reads the first bytes, counts boots in the last page and probes once a second; unplug the module and plug it back while it runs. The checks that count, behind your handler on your board, are listed in Status and limitations . Record the board, the driver commit and the result there.

After every call the target checks the driver's promises and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a failed call returns an Error the enum defines (never one documented as not returned) and T{} ; before EnsureInitialized() no call makes a transfer or a pin write, and InvalidArgument means nothing was sent; nothing is ever written outside the requested range; only Write() changes the array and only SetBlockProtection() changes BP1:BP0; a call never returns Ok for bytes the chip does not hold : an Ok from Read() or Write() matches the chip unless two transfers of the call were tampered (one, with Verify::None ); the input chooses Verify::None or Verify::ReadBack for the reads and writes; with check_write_enable , EnsureInitialized() never returns Ok on a dead bus or with WP tied low unless a transfer was tampered; WP is always parked after a call , unless the last pin write failed; an Ok call leaves the write enable latch clear if it found it clear, unless a transfer was tampered. The fuzzer found two bugs before the first commit, both fixed with a unit test and a regress-* input each: With the write enable latch already set (a WREN before an MCU reset) and WP held low, the identity check's "WREN, then WEN = 1" passed although WP had blocked the WREN. The driver now clears the latch first ( regress-wen-preset-wp-low ). One status read that looked idle (a lost transfer reading 0x00) while a write cycle ran let Read() go ahead; the busy chip ignored both READs, both copies read 0xFF, and Read() returned Ok with wrong bytes. An idle status now counts only when a second read confirms it ( regress-idle-glitch-during-cycle ). # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DAT25040B_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DAT25040B_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_at25040b ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_at25040b -max_total_time = 300 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_at25040b The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_at25040b , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_at25040b/ on GCC and Clang: the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise ( regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request (job Host quality / fuzz ). After the fixes, ten minutes of local fuzzing (9.6 million runs, 451 coverage edges) broke no promise; after the move to spans, the Pin error and ReadRawStatus() , 200 s more (2.28 million runs, 478 edges) broke none.

docs.text: Write(), step by step Figure description and sources Top to bottom, one card per step of Write(); a pill on a card names the error that step can return, and any step that sends a transfer also returns Bus when the transfer fails. The first two steps read the status (until no write cycle runs, confirmed by a second read) and refuse a range that overlaps the block-protected part before anything else is sent. WP is then released, if the port drives it. The band in the middle repeats once per 8-byte page: WREN and a status read that must show WEN = 1, the WRITE, a wait for the write cycle polled every kPollIntervalUs up to Config::write_timeout_us, a status that must show WEN = 0 again (still 1 means the chip ignored the WRITE), and only when the call passes Verify::ReadBack a read-back of the page. After the last page, or the first failure, WP is parked; a failure after WREN also sends WRDI.
